{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Tests

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  Tools_Tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      MAKEFLAGS: "-j 2"
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Build tools unit tests
      run: (cd tools; make all)
    - name: Run tools unit tests
      run: (cd tools; make run_tests)
    - name: Build swig extension and run simple test
      run: (cd python; make testdocker)

  Unit_Tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      MAKEFLAGS: "-j 2"
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Cache Google Test dependency
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: lib/googletest
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-googletest-${{ hashFiles('test/Makefile') }}
    - name: Install the Google test suite
      run: (cd test; make install-googletest)
    - name: Build base unit test
      run: (cd test; make IRac_test)
    - name: Build library unit tests
      run: (cd test; make all)
    - name: Run library unit tests
      run: (cd test; make run)",
  "rationale": "The Unit_Tests job runs `make install-googletest` on every CI run, repeatedly fetching the Google Test dependency. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (measured evidence showing ~6% elapsed savings) supports caching dependency downloads to reduce CI time. Adding an `actions/cache@v4` step before the googletest installation caches the dependency directory, keyed on the test Makefile, so repeated runs reuse the cached dependency while still running the installation and all required tests. All build and test steps are preserved, no permissions are weakened, no new network access or secrets are added, and no deployment/publishing operations are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
